days.title: Variables & Data Types
learningObjectives: Understand the difference between const and let
Work with strings, numbers, and booleans
Use template literals for string interpolation

content.theory:
JavaScript variables are containers for storing data values. In modern JavaScript, we use `const` for values that won't change and `let` for values that will. Understanding when to use each is crucial for writing clean, bug-free code.

**const vs let:**
- `const` - Use for values that won't be reassigned (most of the time)
- `let` - Use for values that will change (counters, accumulators)
- Never use `var` in modern JavaScript

**Data Types:**
- **String**: Text data wrapped in quotes
- **Number**: Integers and decimals (JavaScript doesn't distinguish)
- **Boolean**: true or false values

**Template Literals:**
Template literals use backticks (`) and allow you to embed expressions using ${expression} syntax.

concepts.name: const declaration
concepts.explanation: Creates a read-only reference to a value. The variable identifier cannot be reassigned.

concepts.name: let declaration
concepts.explanation: Creates a mutable variable that can be reassigned.
concepts.example:
let counter = 0;
counter = counter + 1; // This works

concepts.name: Template Literals
concepts.explanation: Allow embedded expressions and multi-line strings using backticks.

codeExamples.title: Basic Variable Usage
codeExamples.explanation: This example shows how to declare variables and use template literals in an n8n Function node context.

codeExamples.title: Adding Timestamp to Data
codeExamples.explanation: This demonstrates how to take input data and enrich it with metadata using modern JavaScript.

practice.title: Create a Data Enricher
practice.instructions:
Create a Function node in n8n that takes input data and adds:
1. A timestamp (current date/time)
2. A unique ID (use Date.now())
3. A status field set to 'processed'
4. Return the enriched data
hints: Use Date.now() for simple numeric IDs
Use the spread operator (...) to copy existing fields

keyTakeaways: Use const by default, let only when you need to reassign
Template literals (`) are more powerful than string concatenation (+)
All n8n Function nodes must return an array of objects with json property
The spread operator (...) is useful for copying object properties

days.title: Arrays & Array Methods
learningObjectives: Use array destructuring for cleaner code

content.theory:
Arrays are ordered collections of values. JavaScript provides powerful methods to transform and filter arrays without writing traditional loops. These methods are essential for working with data in n8n.

**Key Array Methods:**
- `.map()` - Transform each element and return a new array
- `.filter()` - Keep only elements that pass a test
- `.find()` - Get the first element that matches
- `.reduce()` - Combine all elements into a single value

**Why These Matter in n8n:**
When n8n passes data between nodes, it often comes as an array of items. You'll constantly be mapping, filtering, and transforming these arrays.

concepts.name: Array Creation
concepts.explanation: Arrays can be created with square brackets. They can hold any data type.
concepts.example:
const numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
const mixed = ['text', 42, true, { key: 'value' }];

concepts.name: .map() Method
concepts.explanation: Creates a new array by transforming each element. Returns an array of the same length.

concepts.name: .filter() Method
concepts.explanation: Creates a new array with elements that pass a test. May return fewer elements.

concepts.name: .find() Method
concepts.explanation: Returns the first element that matches the condition, or undefined.

codeExamples.title: Filter High-Value Items
codeExamples.explanation: This pattern is common in n8n: get all items, extract json data, filter, then convert back to n8n format.

codeExamples.title: Transform API Response
codeExamples.explanation: Demonstrates chaining .map() to first extract data, then transform it.

codeExamples.title: Find Specific Item
codeExamples.explanation: Shows how to search for a specific item and handle the case when it's not found.

practice.title: Filter Incomplete Todos
practice.instructions:
You receive an array of todo items. Each has:
- id (number)
- task (string)
- completed (boolean)
- priority (string: 'low', 'medium', 'high')

Create a function that:
1. Filters out completed todos
2. Filters to show only 'high' priority items
3. Returns only the task text and id
hints: Chain .filter() twice - once for completed, once for priority
Use .map() at the end to transform to only id and task
Remember: .filter() keeps items where the condition is true

keyTakeaways: .filter() creates a subset based on conditions
These methods don't modify the original array
You can chain multiple array methods together
Arrow functions (=>) make array methods concise

days.title: Objects & JSON

content.theory:
Objects are JavaScript's way of grouping related data together. In n8n, almost everything is an object - API responses, database records, user data. JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is just a string representation of objects.

**Object Basics:**
- Key-value pairs: `{ key: value }`
- Access with dot notation: `obj.key`
- Access with bracket notation: `obj['key']` (useful for dynamic keys)
- Nested objects: objects inside objects

**Why This Matters:**
Every API you call returns JSON. Every node in n8n passes objects. Mastering object manipulation is critical for automation work.

concepts.name: Object Creation
concepts.explanation: Objects store data as key-value pairs enclosed in curly braces.

concepts.name: Accessing Properties
concepts.explanation: Two ways: dot notation (obj.key) or bracket notation (obj['key']).

concepts.name: Nested Objects
concepts.explanation: Objects can contain other objects, creating hierarchical data structures.

concepts.name: Spread Operator
concepts.explanation: The ... operator copies all properties from one object to another.

concepts.name: Object Methods
concepts.explanation: Object.keys(), Object.values(), and Object.entries() help you work with objects.

codeExamples.title: Restructure API Response
codeExamples.explanation: Common pattern: take flat API response and restructure into a more logical format.

codeExamples.title: Flatten Nested Object
codeExamples.explanation: Sometimes APIs nest data too deeply. Flatten it for easier use downstream.

codeExamples.title: Merge Multiple Objects
codeExamples.explanation: Use spread operator to merge data from multiple n8n nodes.

codeExamples.title: Dynamic Key Access
codeExamples.explanation: Bracket notation lets you access properties using variable names.

practice.title: Transform Complex Object
hints: Navigate nested objects with dot notation: apiResponse.data.user.personal.firstName
For isPremium, check both tier and active fields

keyTakeaways: Objects store related data as key-value pairs
Use dot notation for known keys, bracket notation for dynamic keys
Spread operator (...) is powerful for copying and merging objects
Most API responses are nested objects - learn to navigate them
JSON is just a string representation of JavaScript objects
